## Description {#details}

A class template for a doubly linked list forward iterator.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="T">Type of object returned by the iterator.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="N">Type of intrusive node. Must have the public members <b>previous</b> &amp; <b>next</b>.</ParametersListItem>
<ParametersListItem name="U">Type stored in the list, derived from T.</ParametersListItem>
</ParametersList>
This iterator provides an interface similar to <code>std::list::iterator</code> for traversing a doubly linked list. It supports bidirectional iteration and access to the underlying node and value. In a typical doubly linked list, all types are <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-links">double&#95;list&#95;links</Link></code>.

### double&#95;list&#95;iterator() {#ac26720e2d8837ad6e26e2f103bf3e8e3}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class N = T, class U = T&gt;</>}

  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Default constructor. Constructs an iterator pointing to <code>nullptr</code>.

The default constructor for <code><Link to="/docs/api/classes/micro-os-plus/utils/double-list-iterator">double&#95;list&#95;iterator</Link></code> initialises the iterator to a null state, meaning it does not point to any node in the list. This is typically used to create an &quot;end&quot; iterator or to initialise an iterator variable before assigning it to a valid node.


:::info
The internal node pointer is value-initialised (set to <code>nullptr</code>), ensuring that the iterator is safe to use in comparisons and will not dereference an invalid address.
:::

The inequality comparison operator (<code>operator!=</code>) checks whether two iterators point to different nodes in the list by comparing their internal node pointers. This is useful for standard iterator operations, such as determining whether an iterator has reached the end of a range or for loop termination conditions.

  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Dereference operator.

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Reference to the value pointed to by the iterator.
</SectionUser>

The dereference operator (<code>operator&#42;</code>) provides access to the value or object pointed to by the iterator. Internally, it calls <code><Link to="#a4dda1a12bf05e974cc3e6394f28302a0">get&#95;pointer()</Link></code> to obtain a pointer to the underlying value or object associated with the current node in the list, and then dereferences it to return a reference.

This allows the iterator to be used in a manner similar to standard C++ iterators, enabling direct access to the list element for reading or modification.

### operator++() {#a79955aa86c312930d561bfdaa7f8e740}

<MemberDefinition
  template={<>template &lt;class T, class N = T, class U = T&gt;</>}
  prototype={<>double&#95;list&#95;iterator&lt; T, N, U &gt; &amp; micro&#95;os&#95;plus::utils::double&#95;list&#95;iterator&lt; T, N, U &gt;::operator++ ()</>}
  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Pre-increment operator.

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Reference to the incremented iterator.
</SectionUser>

The pre-increment operator (<code>operator++</code>) advances the iterator to the next node in the list. It updates the internal node pointer to point to the node returned by the current node&#39;s <code>next()</code> method. This allows the iterator to traverse the list in the forward direction, following the linked structure.

  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Post-increment operator.

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Iterator before increment.
</SectionUser>

The post-increment operator (<code><Link to="#a60ce68c08d226be1b5ff5bc92e21a4fc">operator++(int)</Link></code>) advances the iterator to the next node in the list, but returns a copy of the iterator as it was before the increment. This allows iteration logic that requires access to the current element before moving to the next one, following the standard C++ iterator semantics for post-increment.

  labels = {["constexpr"]}>
Pre-decrement operator.

<SectionUser title="Returns">
Reference to the decremented iterator.
</SectionUser>

The pre-decrement operator (<code>operator--</code>) moves the iterator to the previous node in the list. It updates the internal node pointer to point to the node returned by the current node&#39;s <code>previous</code> pointer. This enables backward traversal of the list, following the linked structure in reverse.
